note: Primary-source facts that no XBRL or prose extractor can reach. WhiteHawk has filed no 10-K or 10-Q since the 2026-06-10 IPO, so sec_companyfacts.json carries only S-1 fee-table (ffd) concepts and filing_facts carries a single regex-parsed figure. Every row below is read off a table in the 424B4 prospectus and is held to the same source/locator/as-of bar as an extracted fact. Extended 2026-08-11 after the filing extract was restored from 300,000 to 1,283,894 chars (23% -> 100% coverage); the location table, covenants and hedging requirement were all beyond the old truncation point.

facts.rationale: Class B common carries votes and no economic rights, so it is not a claim on value. The Continuing Equity Owners' 3,750,000 OpCo Interests are exchangeable 1:1 into Class A and are the real 14.0% economic claim. The earnout is 25% of the $130.0m Internalization Price payable in OpCo Interests; at the $26.00 IPO price that is 1,250,000 units, diluting the Company to 82.1%.

source.locator: Our Organizational Structure; the Company will own 22,996,579 OpCo Interests (86.0%) and the Continuing Equity Owners 3,750,000 (14.0%)

facts.rationale: Total estimated net proved reserves at 2025-12-31 in MMcfe (177,380 MMcf gas + 3,457 MBbl NGL + 1,392 MBbl oil at 6:1). Of this, 178,544 MMcfe is proved developed producing, 23,066 MMcfe proved developed non-producing and 4,864 MMcfe proved undeveloped. Reserve report prepared by CG&A.

facts.rationale: PV-10 of $293.690m divided by 206,473 MMcfe of total proved reserves = $1.422 per Mcfe. PV-10 is the pre-tax standardized measure discounted at 10% under SEC rules, using trailing-12-month average prices of $3.387/MMBtu Henry Hub and $65.34/bbl WTI, realized at $3.03/Mcf gas, $22.03/bbl NGL and $62.99/bbl oil.

source.locator: SUMMARY RESERVE DATA, WhiteHawk column at December 31, 2025, PV-10: $293,690 thousand against 206,473 MMcfe

facts.rationale: Total gross undeveloped locations at 2025-12-31: Appalachian 2,792, Haynesville 1,581, Mid-Continent 3,952, Other 458. Of these 430 are included in proved reserves; the remaining 8,353 are NOT in the reserve report but were audited and approved by CG&A, the same engineer. This is the inventory the proved book structurally cannot capture: a non-operated mineral owner cannot commit to a development plan, so SEC rules bar it from booking PUDs, which is why proved is 98% PD / 2% PUD.

source.locator: Gross and net locations by region or basin table, as of December 31, 2025; footnote (3) 'audited and approved by CG&A'

facts.rationale: Net undeveloped location count: Appalachian 8.7, Haynesville 3.1, Mid-Continent 14.1, Other 2.1. Mid-Continent is 50% of net locations but has 9,314 ft average laterals against 13,246 ft in Appalachia and materially lower EUR per foot, so net locations must be basin-weighted rather than treated uniformly.

source.locator: Gross and net locations by region or basin table, Net Undeveloped Location Count column, as of December 31, 2025

facts.rationale: Note Purchase Agreement requires Consolidated Total Net Leverage Ratio <= 3.50x from the quarter ending 2026-06-30, Asset Coverage Ratio >= 1.00x and Liquidity Percentage >= 10%. The Revolving Credit Facility carries a 3.00x Leverage Ratio test. Restricted payments including dividends require pro forma Consolidated Total Net Leverage below 2.00x. Against ~$58-64m net debt and $64.405m pro forma Adjusted EBITDA, actual leverage is ~0.9-1.0x -- inside every test including the dividend gate.

source.locator: Description of Material Indebtedness -- Financial Covenants; restricted payments condition (Z) Consolidated Total Net Leverage Ratio < 2.00 to 1.00

facts.rationale: The Note Purchase Agreement REQUIRES fixed-price swaps on at least 75% of reasonably anticipated PDP production for the 36 months following closing, and at least 50% for the 36 months following each subsequent fiscal quarter. Royalty revenue is therefore NOT the unhedged commodity pass-through the deep dive describes: 50-75% of producing volumes are contractually locked on a rolling three-year basis. This dampens both the downside and the gas-price upside the market appears to be pricing.

source.locator: Description of Material Indebtedness -- Note Purchase Agreement, hedging covenant
